title: W-13, W-21, W-22, W-23: memory and disk residue hardening (parsed secrets as strings, core dumps, free pages, zeroing, inherited ACLs)
description: Source: the consolidated pre-public security review (opum-doc, 2026-10-30), reviewed at b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d; tracked under ODOC-552 and parent WCLI-95. Report id: W-13, W-21, W-22, W-23 (low and info). parseVaultState turns every stored secret into immutable JS strings on every vault open, plaintext.fill never reaches them, the vault key and state stay alive across the network exchange, and reporting.ts:238-240 claims an invariant the code does not have; no secure_delete pragma leaves old revisions in free pages; several key, passphrase and plaintext copies and one transport buffer are not zeroed; files Ward did not create keep an inherited ACL on a pre-existing ~/.ward. Only a same-user memory reader exploits these (conceded); zeroing is best effort by ADR 0002.

acceptanceCriteria.text: RLIMIT_CORE is set to 0 at startup and state references are dropped before the send
PRAGMA secure_delete = ON is set, or the decision not to is recorded
Each listed copy is zeroed in a finally block and the transport comment about the one credential buffer is corrected
The inherited-ACL caveat for files Ward did not create is documented or stripped on first use
